hooks.prompt:
Decide whether Claude may stop at the end of this turn. The hook input is:
$ARGUMENTS

STEP 1 - re-entry guard. If the hook input has "stop_hook_active": true, allow the stop. This rule is absolute: nothing below overrides it, and you do not evaluate anything else.

STEP 2 - allow the stop if ANY of these is true. "This turn" means everything since the user's most recent typed message (not system reminders, tool results, task notifications or stop-hook feedback).
a. This turn has no git commit, git push, gh pr create, gh pr merge or gh api PATCH of a pull request.
b. Claude's final message ends by asking the user a question or waiting for the user's decision.
c. Claude's final message says it is waiting on background work it started (CI, a reviewer agent, a test run) before merging.

STEP 3 - the project's review rule. Each pull request gets ONE consolidated reviewer agent over its diff. After every later commit on that PR, the same reviewer re-checks only the new commits. A PR is merged only when that reviewer's latest verdict is CLEAN and its CI is green. Per-file-type reviewers (ts-principal, qa-engineer, doc-expert, security-reviewer, python-principal, go-principal, architect) are NOT required, and their absence is never a reason to block.

Block only if one of these happened this turn:
- Claude merged a PR (gh pr merge) whose latest reviewer verdict, as shown in the transcript, was not CLEAN or whose CI was not green.
- Claude opened a PR or pushed commits to one, and its final message presents that work as finished without a reviewer having been started or re-asked on those commits.
When you block, the reason names the PR and exactly what is missing, in one or two sentences.

In every other case, allow the stop.
